question.text: What is the Online Dispute Resolution (ODR) mechanism introduced by SEBI for mutual fund investor grievances?

answer.text: A replacement for SCORES that handles all SEBI-related complaints

A digital mechanism for resolution of investor complaints and disputes through conciliation and arbitration via SEBI-empaneled ODR institutions, accessible after initial complaint resolution attempts fail
An internal complaint mechanism within each AMC for employee grievances
A court-based system for filing civil suits against mutual fund AMCs

explanation.text: The Logic: The Online Dispute Resolution (ODR) framework introduced by SEBI is a digital mechanism that enables investors to resolve unresolved complaints and disputes against listed companies and registered intermediaries through online conciliation and online arbitration administered by SEBI-empanelled ODR institutions. Typically, an investor first raises the complaint directly with the entity and then through SCORES; if the grievance remains unresolved, the investor may escalate to ODR for time-bound conciliation and, where necessary, arbitration. The process is end-to-end digital, designed to be faster and lower-cost than traditional litigation. The Trap: "A replacement for SCORES that handles all SEBI-related complaints" is incorrect — ODR sits alongside SCORES as an escalation/resolution layer, not as a replacement covering every SEBI complaint type. "An internal complaint mechanism within each AMC" confuses ODR with the entity's own grievance redressal cell. "A court-based system" is the opposite of ODR's design, which uses alternative dispute resolution (conciliation and arbitration), not the formal court process. Note: The cited NISM Series V-A workbook pages discuss SCORES, investor grievance redressal, payment platforms and related operational mechanics, but the searches conducted for the audit did not find an Online Dispute Resolution / conciliation / arbitration mechanism statement on those Series V-A pages. The framing above is presented as general SEBI regulatory knowledge of the ODR mechanism applicable to securities-market disputes, not as a workbook-page citation.
